name: SQL statement built by string concatenation
description: A SQL statement is assembled from string literals and concatenated values. In VB6 this is the classic SQL injection pattern (ADODB/DAO Execute, Recordset.Open, CommandText).
recommendation: Use ADODB.Command with Parameters (adCmdText/adCmdStoredProc) or validate and escape the concatenated values.
must-match: sql = "SELECT UserId, Role FROM Users WHERE Login = '" & txtUser.Text & "'"
gConn.Execute "DELETE FROM Orders WHERE OrderNo = " & orderNo
must-not-match: cmd.CommandText = "SELECT UserId FROM Users WHERE Login = ?"

name: Shell command built from variables
description: Shell() is called with a command line that is not a fixed string literal. If any part of it comes from user input, files or the database, arbitrary commands can be executed.
recommendation: Avoid Shell for anything but fixed commands. Validate arguments against an allow-list and quote them; prefer ShellExecute with a fixed verb and a validated file path.

name: Process execution through WScript.Shell, Shell.Application or ShellExecute
description: The code starts external processes through Windows Script Host, the Shell automation object or the ShellExecute API. Paths and verbs derived from untrusted data lead to command or file execution.
recommendation: Review every call site: fix the verb, validate the target path against an allow-list and never pass user controlled strings as the file or parameters argument.
must-match:
Set wsh = CreateObject("WScript.Shell")
ShellExecute 0, "open", exportDir, vbNullString, vbNullString, 1
must-not-match: Public Declare Function ShellExecute Lib "shell32.dll" Alias "ShellExecuteA" (ByVal hwnd As Long) As Long

name: Dynamic script execution through the Microsoft Script Control
description: MSScriptControl evaluates or executes VBScript/JScript supplied at runtime. Script text that originates from users, files or database tables is executed with the privileges of the application.
recommendation: Replace runtime script evaluation with a fixed expression parser or a whitelist of named rules; never execute script text from untrusted sources.

name: Hard-coded credential or secret
description: A password, key or token is embedded as a constant or inside a connection string. VB6 binaries are trivially decompiled with string tools, so such secrets are effectively public.
recommendation: Move secrets to a protected configuration store (DPAPI protected file, Windows Credential Manager) or use integrated Windows authentication for database connections.

name: Connection string keeps credentials in memory (Persist Security Info=True)
description: With Persist Security Info=True the OLE DB provider keeps the password in the connection object, where it can be read back through ConnectionString and ends up in logs and crash dumps.
recommendation: Set Persist Security Info=False (the default) or use integrated security.

name: Broken or weak cryptographic algorithm
description: Use of MD2/MD4/MD5, RC2/RC4, DES or a hand-rolled XOR cipher was found. These algorithms do not provide confidentiality or integrity against a current attacker.
recommendation: Use CryptoAPI/CNG with AES (CALG_AES_256) and SHA-256 (CALG_SHA_256), or delegate cryptography to a maintained component. Never implement XOR 'encryption'.
must-match: Public Function XorEncrypt(ByVal plainText As String, ByVal key As String) As String

name: SHA-1 hash algorithm
description: SHA-1 is no longer collision resistant and must not be used for signatures, certificates or password hashing.
recommendation: Use CALG_SHA_256 or stronger.

name: Rnd() used for a security-relevant value
description: The VB6 Rnd() generator is a predictable linear congruential generator seeded from the system clock. Tokens, passwords, salts or session identifiers derived from it can be guessed.
recommendation: Use CryptGenRandom (advapi32) or BCryptGenRandom to generate security-relevant random values.
must-match:
Public Function NewSessionToken() As String
    Randomize
    NewSessionToken = Hex$(CLng(Rnd * 2147483647))
End Function

name: SendKeys keystroke injection
description: SendKeys types keystrokes into whichever window has the focus. It is unreliable, can leak credentials into the wrong application and is frequently used to script logins into other programs.
recommendation: Use the target application's API or automation interface. Never transmit credentials through SendKeys.

name: Errors silently ignored (On Error Resume Next)
description: On Error Resume Next suppresses every runtime error in the procedure. Failed authentication checks, failed file operations and failed database calls continue as if they had succeeded.
recommendation: Use structured On Error GoTo handlers and check Err.Number after calls that may fail; keep the Resume Next scope as small as possible.

name: File system operation with a dynamic path
description: Kill, FileCopy, RmDir, MkDir, ChDir or Open ... For Input/Output/Append/Binary is called with a path assembled at runtime. Path traversal ('..\') or wildcard characters in user data can destroy or expose files outside the intended folder.
recommendation: Canonicalise the path, reject '..' and wildcards, and confirm the result lies inside an allowed base directory before performing the operation.
must-match: Open m_logPath & "\" & user & ".log" For Append As #fh

name: TLS certificate errors ignored
description: ServerXMLHTTP option 2 (SXH_OPTION_IGNORE_SERVER_SSL_CERT_ERROR_FLAGS) or WinHttpRequest option 4 (SslErrorIgnoreFlags) is set to ignore certificate errors. This disables server authentication and enables man-in-the-middle attacks.
recommendation: Remove the option and install a trusted certificate on the server; fix the trust chain instead of ignoring it.

name: XML parser resolves external entities
description: MSXML is configured to resolve external entities or to allow DTDs. Attacker supplied XML can then read local files or reach internal network services (XXE).
recommendation: Leave resolveExternals at False, set ProhibitDTD to True and prefer MSXML 6.0.

name: Raw socket communication through the Winsock control
description: The Microsoft Winsock control sends and receives data over plain TCP/UDP without transport encryption or peer authentication.
recommendation: Tunnel the protocol through TLS (e.g. stunnel, a TLS-terminating proxy) or replace the control with WinHTTP over HTTPS.

name: Legacy Internet Transfer Control (MSINET) with a dynamic URL
description: The Internet Transfer Control is a legacy HTTP/FTP client without configurable TLS and certificate validation. Passing runtime URLs to OpenURL/Execute additionally enables server-side request forgery.
recommendation: Replace MSINET with WinHTTP over HTTPS and validate URLs against an allow-list of hosts.

name: Unsafe memory access (CopyMemory/RtlMoveMemory, VarPtr/StrPtr/ObjPtr)
description: Direct memory copies and raw pointers bypass VB6's bounds checking. Wrong lengths or stale pointers corrupt memory and can be exploitable.
recommendation: Review each call for correct buffer sizes and lifetimes; prefer typed VB6 constructs (arrays, LSet, user-defined types) where possible.
must-not-match: Public Declare Sub CopyMemory Lib "kernel32" Alias "RtlMoveMemory" (Destination As Any, Source As Any, ByVal Length As Long)

name: Secret stored in or read from the registry in clear text
description: SaveSetting/GetSetting store values unencrypted under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\VB and VBA Program Settings. Passwords and tokens stored there are readable by any process running as the user.
recommendation: Protect the value with DPAPI (CryptProtectData) before storing it, or use the Windows Credential Manager.
must-not-match: Public Declare Function RegSetValueEx Lib "advapi32.dll" Alias "RegSetValueExA" (ByVal hKey As Long, ByVal lpPassword As String) As Long

name: Untrusted input source (command line, environment, InputBox)
description: Command$, Environ$ and InputBox return attacker influenced data. Track where the value flows: SQL statements, Shell commands, file paths and script evaluation are the critical sinks.
recommendation: Validate the value immediately against the expected format and treat it as untrusted in every sink.

name: LoadLibrary with a bare DLL name (DLL search order hijacking)
description: LoadLibrary is called with a file name without a full path. Windows searches the application directory, the current directory and PATH, so a planted DLL of the same name gets loaded.
recommendation: Pass a fully qualified path (App.Path based) and use LoadLibraryEx with LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_* flags.

name: Reference to an out-of-support or superseded component
description: The project references a Microsoft component that no longer receives security updates (MSXML 2.x/4.x/5, DAO 3.5, CAPICOM, VB5 runtime) or that has been superseded (Common Controls 5.0).
recommendation: Migrate to the supported successor: MSXML 6.0, DAO 3.6/ACE, CNG instead of CAPICOM, MSCOMCTL.OCX (Common Controls 6.0 SP6).

name: Internal error details shown to the user
description: Err.Description is displayed in a message box. Provider error texts reveal SQL statements, table names, file paths and server names.
recommendation: Log the technical details and show the user a generic message with a correlation id.
